summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate (Rochester Institute of Technology) with robotic systems hands-on experience across ROS2 kinematics, sensor integration, and closed-loop actuator control. Built and debugged physical robot systems end-to-end — PWM-driven servo/actuator control, time-of-flight sensors, and interrupt-driven override for safe intervention — while resolving integration failures through systematic mechanical and electrical troubleshooting. Comfortable working hands-on with cabling, wiring, and PCB-level hardware in lab and national-competition robotics environments, with Python scripting for data acquisition and logging.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and sensor/actuator integration, including mechanical troubleshooting and electrical debugging.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback, including cabling and connector wiring.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI (PyQt/Matplotlib) for real-time data acquisition, monitoring, and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on a physical UR5e via the UR ROS 2 driver; AL5B repeatability measured at <2mm over 10 trials.
Derived DH tables and hand-computed full forward kinematic chains (0T6) for a 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B; validated against MoveIt and RViz URDF models in ROS 2 Humble and ROS Noetic.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo actuator control (PWM) with interrupt-driven UART command handling and real-time user override for safe intervention — pause/stop/reset of live actuator motion.
Integrated FreeRTOS-based multi-threaded task coordination (mutexes) with VL53L0X time-of-flight sensing and OLED distance visualization for closed-loop object tracking.
Deployed YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson for real-time object detection and tracking, streaming control commands to an STM32 actuator controller over UART.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) by identifying recurring failure patterns; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.

Deployed the Jetson-side arm bridge as a systemd service (auto-restart with backoff, non-root isolation) with static IP networking for reliable multi-device registration; configured XRDP for remote administration of the headless Jetson.

awards: Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
